title: proxy-driven mini-canaries for locked model revisions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: provide a lightweight, reproducible canary/A-B validation path for model revisions that are pinned to customer routes. The approach routes a small fraction of live traffic through a transparent proxy sidecar ("traffic sidecar") that duplicates requests and sends a trimmed, rate-limited copy to the candidate revision without changing primary routing. This lets us gather latency, token-cost, and semantic-quality comparisons against production control responses while guaranteeing no user-facing regressions and preserving pin semantics.
background_and_motivation: We currently use shadowing and staged traffic templates, but teams have requested: (1) a non-invasive traffic duplication path that respects pins and per-route quotas, (2) more control over sampling logic at edge (region/cohort/customers), and (3) the ability to attach lightweight synthetic latency/fault injection for resilience testing. Traffic sidecars live at the routing layer, augmenting existing pin semantics while enabling A/B-type experiments for pinned revisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ability to enable a traffic-sidecar for a pinned revision with a single API flag on the pin. 2) Duplication is opt-in; production responses are never replaced. 3) Captured metrics: token count, p95 latency delta, semantic drift score (via eval probes), error rates. 4) Dashboard shows side-by-side comparison for a selected 24h window and allows cohort filtering. 5) Rollback triggers: if p95 latency delta > 50ms AND quality regression > 2% on a configured prompt set, an automated alert and optional pause is triggered.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev/prototype): local proxy simulation and unit tests (ENG). Phase 1 (internal dogfooding): enable on <10 internal routes with synthetic prompts and no customer traffic. Phase 2 (controlled production): enable traffic-sidecar on 1% sample for non-sensitive customers with full telemetry. Phase 3 (widen): increase to 5-10% and add cohort splits and A/B evaluation tooling. Final: promote to self-serve toggle in Console for org-admins once telemetry reliability and gating infra are stable.
metrics_and_gates: Primary metrics: p95 latency delta (candidate vs control), token cost delta per request, semantic-match score from eval-set, error rate delta. Gate conditions: automatic pause when any of the following occur within a 15-minute window for the canary cohort - latency delta > 50ms AND semantic-match drop > 2%; error rate increase > 0.5% absolute; sustained token-cost increase > 12% leading to projected >$X/day. Manual gate: PM/Eng review required for widening beyond 10%.
implementation_notes: - Sidecar will be implemented as a stateless proxy in the routing plane; compatible with both hosted and dedicated. - Use existing KV-caching hooks to ensure duplicated requests reuse cache keys to avoid unnecessary compute. - Candidate requests are annotated and routed to a 'canary' inference pool to avoid interfering with capacity-based routing. - Telemetry emitted to metrics pipeline with 'sidecar.' prefix. - Feature flag gated; Console will show toggle and cohort rules. - Requires runtime kernel selection to be compatible with pinned quantized variants; ENG to validate.
security_and_compliance_considerations: Traffic duplication must not expose customer-provided PII to non-authorized pools. For private deployments, sidecar will default to disabled and must honor VPC boundaries. KMS constraints apply for any archived requests; retention follows org policy. Security review scheduled (see links).

open_questions_and_risks: 1) How to compute semantic-match score consistently across model families (embedding vs logit-based signals)? 2) Cost of capturing full request payloads for offline analysis in high-QPS routes. 3) Edge case: pinned routes with hard SLAs—should we disallow sidecars by default? Proposed mitigation: require admin consent and add per-route opt-out list.
